Planting tomatoes in a garden bed

To plant tomatoes in a garden bed, first select a site that gets plenty of sun, at least 6 to 8 hours each day. This is crucial because tomatoes need a lot of light to grow strong and produce fruit. Next, prepare the soil by mixing in a few inches of compost or well-rotted manure. This enriches the soil with nutrients that the tomatoes will need to grow. Make small holes in the soil, spaced about 24 to 36 inches apart, depending on the variety of tomato. This spacing helps ensure each plant has enough room to grow without competing for resources. Gently place a tomato plant into each hole, with the stem buried up to the first set of leaves. Burying the stem helps the plant produce more roots, which will make it stronger.
